newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed says Midwest slowing due to autos.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed says Midwest slowing due to autos.

text.p: A slowdown in the manufacturing sector of the midwest U.S. economy can be attributed to a drop in automobile sales, according to an official at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.
William Strauss, an economist at the Chicago Fed, spoke to Reuters Financial Television following the release of the regional Fed bank's midwest manufacturing index.
The Chicago Fed Midwest Manufacturing Index fell 0.1 percent in May to 121.6, the first decline in seven months, indicating a slight slowdown in regional industrial activity.
Turning to the consumer sector in his region, Strauss said, "I think maybe consumers are taking a little bit of a breather" following the torrid pace of spending seen in the first quarter.
Strauss also said the midwest was experiencing "extremely tight" labor markets, which were sparking mild wage pressures.
He added, however, that perceived gains in industry productiving were likely to offset the impact of those salary increases on overall inflation indexes.
The Chicago Fed covers the seventh U.S. economic district, which includes Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, and Wisconsin.
